questions.q: Why are ProductKey, OrderDateKey, TerritoryKey, and CustomerKey declared as plain INT columns on dw.FactProductSales, with no REFERENCES clause, at this point in the build?
options: Because SQL Server does not support foreign keys on MONEY columns
Because the dimension tables they would reference (dw.DimProduct, dw.DimDate, dw.DimTerritory, dw.DimCustomer) don't exist yet
Because surrogate keys are never allowed to have foreign key constraints
Because Power BI requires foreign keys to be added after publishing
questions.explain: A REFERENCES constraint against a table that doesn't exist yet fails immediately in SQL Server. The constraints get added in Lesson 6, once every dimension is built and populated.

questions.q: Which two columns on dw.FactProductSales are degenerate dimensions, and why?
options: ProductKey and CustomerKey, because they are surrogate keys
OrderQty and LineTotal, because they are measures
SalesOrderID and SalesOrderDetailID, because they identify the exact source row with no attributes worth their own dimension table
OrderDateKey and TerritoryKey, because they reference dw.DimDate
questions.explain: SalesOrderID and SalesOrderDetailID trace a warehouse row back to its exact Sales.SalesOrderDetail source row, without needing a separate dimension table.

questions.q: Why is LineTotal loaded into the warehouse as an already-computed, stored value instead of being recalculated by each front-end from UnitPrice and UnitPriceDiscount?
options: MONEY columns cannot store computed values

Recalculating it independently in Power BI, Tableau, and Excel risks a rounding or logic difference between the three, which is exactly the kind of discrepancy this capstone's architecture is built to prevent
UnitPrice and UnitPriceDiscount don't actually exist in AdventureWorks2012
Because Finance specifically forbids computed columns
questions.explain: LineTotal is already a computed column in the OLTP source; storing that same computed value once in the warehouse means all three front-ends see the identical number instead of three independently-derived ones.

questions.q: What is the real formula behind Sales.SalesOrderDetail.LineTotal in AdventureWorks2012?
options: OrderQty + UnitPrice
UnitPrice * (1 - UnitPriceDiscount) * OrderQty
UnitPrice / OrderQty
A fixed per-product flat rate
questions.explain: LineTotal is a computed column equal to UnitPrice times (1 minus UnitPriceDiscount) times OrderQty.

questions.q: What is the primary key of dw.FactProductSales, and what kind of key is it?
options: SalesOrderID — a natural key carried over from the source
SalesLineKey — a new IDENTITY surrogate key generated by the warehouse itself
ProductKey — a foreign key to dw.DimProduct
There is no primary key on a fact table by design
questions.explain: SalesLineKey is an IDENTITY(1,1) surrogate key, generated by the warehouse itself — it has no meaning in the source system.
